long_biography.plain_text:
Location work on I Spy exposed Fouad Said to the cost of moving cameras, generators and crews between countries. He compressed those functions into a cargo-plane-ready van, building an experimental model with his own money. When it failed technically, producer Sheldon Leonard supplied a personal loan for the replacement that became the first successful Cinemobile.

The system cut setup time, crew requirements and location costs, allowing Said's company to grow from television work into major films. An Academy Scientific and Engineering Award recognised the design. Said then expanded from providing equipment into film production, using the same mobile infrastructure to challenge the fixed-studio model.

uncertainties.detail: Mr is already correctly stored in the dedicated title field, while the source display name redundantly embeds it. The dossier proposes Fouad Said as the display name and leaves the title field unchanged. The report-layer last-name string also embeds the full titled name, but it is not an editable personal-detail field in this dossier.

Academic bibliographic sources use Ahmed Fouad Said, while contemporary public, corporate, Academy and investment sources use Fouad Said or Fouad Sa'id. The evidence does not establish whether Ahmed should be stored as a middle name or whether Fouad is the preferred component of a differently ordered formal name, so no middle-name proposal is made.

The source record and academic histories give 1933, while a 1971 age statement and 1973 Variety profile imply approximately 1934 or 1935. Variety names Cairo as the birthplace, but the same profile conflicts on year. The existing year remains unchanged; day, month and city remain unproposed pending stronger primary evidence.

Fouad Es-Said of Transmed, Wafic Saïd, software researcher Ahmed Fouad Said and other name matches are distinct people. Only sources matching the target's Egyptian film background, Cinemobile work, birth era and Geneva investment context inform the dossier.

Sources document Said's co-chairmanship of a family investment trust and later investor identity, but do not publish his current personal percentage in that structure. ACE & Company was founded and managed separately; its assets under management and portfolio-company values are not attributed to Fouad Said personally.

The Taft acquisition involved company shares, stock consideration and performance-dependent payments. These transaction figures establish the wealth mechanism but are not treated as a direct statement of Said's enduring personal net worth.

No exact personal LinkedIn or Instagram met the verification threshold. A historical fouadsaid.com domain is cited by older reference pages but currently fails to load, so no personal or company website is proposed.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, private-family trivia and vessel research were excluded. Family relationships appear only where needed to explain formative film access, control of the investment structure or identity disambiguation.
